title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Terintambwe Mw'isi Itotahaye programme will work in Gasagara District, Rwanda. It aims to contribute to Concern Burundi and Concern Rwanda's Green Graduation thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to ensure households can sustainably meet their basic needs and have improved coping strategies through strengthened livelihoods which place value on the natural environment. The programme will support over 147,220 people living in extreme poor households, including landless, female-headed households, households with disabled members, Batwa community (ethnic minority) . This will be done through support to gain the necessary technical and business skills and financial literacy to be able to set up a suitable livelihood, improved human capital through coaching, mentoring and various lifeskills training, participation in gender transformative dialogue sessions and environmental enhancement and low carbon development measures are undertaken.. DRR 1: The program has enhanced the resilience og HHs to shocks and disasters by increasing financial security and, thus, reducing dependence on harmful livelihood coping strategies. Aid to Environment 1: Concern’s Green Graduation programme added a 5th pillar to the traditional graduation model - the ‘green’ aspect which aims to improve environmental protection and stability through awareness raising, capacity building, assessing environmental impacts, reducing and managing environmental risks and increasing natural assets. Capacity Building 1: Participants' capacity is built through training such as on financial management, vocational skills, disaster and climate risk management, gender transformation, business skills, and environmental sustainability. Gender Equality 1: : a gender lens is applied at every stage and a gender transformative approach is taken to tackle harmful gender norms, attitudes and practices. Nutrition 1: Through increased financial security and messaging on nutrition, the nutritional status of HHs is improved.
